# The assistant's tools

<!-- purpose: What the assistant can ask SWCraft to do, tool by tool, and what it cannot do to your files -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

The assistant does not edit your files. It asks SWCraft to do things, and the things it can ask for are exactly the ones below — there is no other way in. Reading this page is how you find out what the assistant is able to do for you, and what it is structurally unable to do to you.

The first four are the whole editing surface. Three of them only answer questions; the fourth is the single way your model is ever written, and it writes a whole proposal at once or nothing at all, after you have seen the exact list of changes. The rest answer a question about the model or the guide, or run a check, a build, or an exchange with another tool. None of them touches a model file — but the ones that build or export do write the files SWCraft generates *from* the model, the AUTOSAR output among them, which is work you can always run again.

They are listed in the order the server offers them, each with the arguments the assistant fills in when it calls one.

| Tool | What it is for |
|---|---|
| [`discover`](#discover) | Describe the model schema, with the baseline token — use when you need a field's meaning or a baseline token. |
| [`read`](#read) | Read the model map, a layer, elements or a field — use when asked what exists or what the model holds. |
| [`find`](#find) | Find addresses by name, requirements by topic, or a requirement's candidates — use when unsure of a name. |
| [`change_set`](#change_set) | Create, update or remove model elements — use when the user asks to add, change, connect, move, delete or link. |
| [`model_diff`](#model_diff) | Summarise, then show, what changed between two model revisions — use when the user asks what changed. |
| [`impact_of`](#impact_of) | Count, then list, what an element affects or depends on — use when the user asks what a change would touch. |
| [`resource_report`](#resource_report) | Report core and memory load, one resource's consumers, or whether an amount fits — use when asked about room. |
| [`architecture_metrics`](#architecture_metrics) | Report the architecture's state and where it is heading — use when asked about coupling, cohesion or trends. |
| [`guide`](#guide) | Read the SWCraft user guide — use when asked how something is done in SWCraft, or what a refusal means. |
| [`build`](#build) | Build the ARXML, diagrams and needs.json outputs — use when the user asks to generate or build the outputs. |
| [`validate`](#validate) | Validate the model and its ARXML (by XSD if configured) — use when asked to check, validate or run check-model. |
| [`export_component`](#export_component) | Export one component, or every component, as ARXML — use when the user asks to export a component or all of them. |
| [`import_component`](#import_component) | Plan the import of a component from an ARXML export — use when the user asks to import a component. |

## `discover` { #discover }

<!-- purpose: What the `discover` tool does, and the arguments the assistant fills in to call it -->

Describe the model schema, with the baseline token — use when you need a field's meaning or a baseline token.

| Argument | Accepted value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | text | optional |
| `form` | text | optional |

## `read` { #read }

<!-- purpose: What the `read` tool does, and the arguments the assistant fills in to call it -->

Read the model map, a layer, elements or a field — use when asked what exists or what the model holds.

| Argument | Accepted value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `address` | a structured value | optional |
| `addresses` | a list, each entry a structured value | optional |
| `form` | text | optional |
| `where` | a list, each entry a structured value | optional |
| `limit` | a whole number | optional |
| `after` | text or a structured value | optional |
| `members` | text | optional |
| `derived` | a list, each entry text | optional |
| `join` | a list, each entry a structured value | optional |

## `find` { #find }

<!-- purpose: What the `find` tool does, and the arguments the assistant fills in to call it -->

Find addresses by name, requirements by topic, or a requirement's candidates — use when unsure of a name.

| Argument | Accepted value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `names` | a list, each entry text | optional |
| `text` | text | optional |
| `for_requirement` | text | optional |
| `candidates` | a whole number | optional |

## `change_set` { #change_set }

<!-- purpose: What the `change_set` tool does, and the arguments the assistant fills in to call it -->

Create, update or remove model elements — use when the user asks to add, change, connect, move, delete or link.

| Argument | Accepted value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | text | required |
| `operations` | a list, each entry a structured value | required |
| `intent` | text | optional |
| `complete` | `true` or `false` | optional — `false` when you leave it out |

## `model_diff` { #model_diff }

<!-- purpose: What the `model_diff` tool does, and the arguments the assistant fills in to call it -->

Summarise, then show, what changed between two model revisions — use when the user asks what changed.

| Argument | Accepted value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `rev_a` | text | optional — `HEAD` when you leave it out |
| `rev_b` | text | optional — `""` when you leave it out |
| `form` | text | optional — `summary` when you leave it out |

## `impact_of` { #impact_of }

<!-- purpose: What the `impact_of` tool does, and the arguments the assistant fills in to call it -->

Count, then list, what an element affects or depends on — use when the user asks what a change would touch.

| Argument | Accepted value | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | required |
| `form` | text | optional — `summary` when you leave it out |
| `direction` | text | optional — `dependents` when you leave it out |
| `depth` | a whole number | optional |
| `limit` | a whole number | optional |
| `after` | text | optional |
